# lucid-search

> Zero-dependency library (ESM, CommonJS, UMD) that finds literal, case-insensitive matches in a string, ignoring accents (by default in findRanges) and, optionally, typos, and returns their positions. A ranking score is included.

In React, Vue or any framework, render toSegments output as elements; highlight() is for plain HTML strings only.

import { findRanges, toSegments, search, highlight, score } from 'lucid-search';

## Rendering matches in a UI

### findRanges(haystack: string, query: string | string[], options?: { normalize?: boolean = true, typos?: number = 0 }): { start, end }[]
Sorted, merged Ranges into the original haystack; accent- and ligature-insensitive by default. Query split on whitespace only.
typos: max Typos per term (insert, delete, replace, or swap of two adjacent letters), capped at one per 4 letters; terms over 32 letters match exactly.
Throws TypeError on non-string haystack or invalid query.

### toSegments(haystack: string, ranges: Range[]): { text, match }[]
Joined, the segments rebuild the haystack exactly. Render match segments with your own elements (no HTML string).

## Searching from an agent or tool call

### search(haystack: string, query: string | string[], options?: { normalize?: boolean })
Returns { matches: { start, end, text, term }[], missing: string[] }.
- haystack.slice(start, end) === text. Matches are sorted by start and never overlap; the longer term wins.
- query is literal (no regex). A string is split on whitespace . - _ into terms; pass an array to keep terms intact.
- missing = terms found nowhere, in the caller's order. Array terms are used exactly as given (spaces included); case-only duplicates collapse to the first spelling.
- normalize: true ignores accents the same way findRanges does (creme -> Crème, strasse -> Straße, final -> ﬁnal) without shifting positions.
- Throws TypeError on non-string haystack or invalid query. Empty query -> { matches: [], missing: [] }.

### highlight(haystack: string, matches: Match[], options?: { el?: string = 'span', cssClass?: string = 'matched' })
Returns HTML: the haystack HTML-escaped, each match wrapped in <el class="cssClass">. Pass matches as search returned them.

## score(haystack: string, ranges: Range[]): number
Higher = better fit. Takes findRanges results or search matches. Use to sort several haystacks searched with the same query.

## Examples
toSegments(haystack, findRanges(haystack, query, { typos: 1 })).map((segment, i) => segment.match ? <mark key={i}>{segment.text}</mark> : segment.text) // React
search('The lazy dog', 'the cat') // { matches: [{ start: 0, end: 3, text: 'The', term: 'the' }], missing: ['cat'] }
highlight('a < dog', search('a < dog', 'dog').matches) // 'a &lt; <span class="matched">dog</span>'
docs.sort((a, b) => score(b, findRanges(b, q)) - score(a, findRanges(a, q))) // best first
const context = matches.map(m => text.slice(Math.max(0, m.start - 80), m.end + 80));
